Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

import os,glob,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])   # this instance's own log: the folder keeps every earlier one's
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))

def solid_edges(g,R,C,i,j,line):
    r0,r1,c0,c1=R[i],R[i+1],C[j],C[j+1]
    es=[(g[r0][c0],g[r0][c1]),(g[r1][c0],g[r1][c1]),(g[r0][c0],g[r1][c0]),(g[r0][c1],g[r1][c1])]
    return [a for a,b in es if a==b and a!=line]
def corners_of(g,R,C,i,j,line):
    r0,r1,c0,c1=R[i],R[i+1],C[j],C[j+1]
    return [g[r0][c0],g[r0][c1],g[r1][c0],g[r1][c1]]
h,w=len(T),len(T[0])
cnt=Counter(x for r in T for x in r)
line=cnt.most_common(2)[1][0]; interior=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
R=[r for r in range(h) if sum(x==line for x in T[r])>w/2]
C=[c for c in range(w) if sum(T[r][c]==line for r in range(h))>h/2]
print(R,C)
for i in range(len(R)-1):
    for j in range(len(C)-1):
        cs=corners_of(T,R,C,i,j,line); se=solid_edges(T,R,C,i,j,line)
        cc=Counter(se).most_common(1)
        e3=cc[0][0] if cc and cc[0][1]>=3 else interior
        nc=Counter(x for x in cs if x!=line).most_common(1)
        c3=nc[0][0] if nc and nc[0][1]>=3 else interior
        c4=cs[0] if cs[0]!=line and all(x==cs[0] for x in cs) else interior
        if not(e3==c3==c4):
            print(i,j,cs,se,'e3',e3,'c3',c3,'c4',c4)

def transform(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in g for x in r)
    line=cnt.most_common(2)[1][0]; interior=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    R=[r for r in range(h) if sum(x==line for x in g[r])>w/2]
    C=[c for c in range(w) if sum(g[r][c]==line for r in range(h))>h/2]
    out=[]
    for i in range(len(R)-1):
        row=[]
        for j in range(len(C)-1):
            cs=[g[R[i+a]][C[j+b]] for a in (0,1) for b in (0,1)]
            cc=Counter(x for x in cs if x!=line).most_common(1)
            row.append(cc[0][0] if len(cs)==len([x for x in cs if x!=line]) and cc[0][1]>=3 else interior)
        out.append(row)
    return out

import re
# re-parse the three demo pairs + test from raw log, using the label positions
labels = [(m.start(), m.group(1), m.group(2)) for m in re.finditer(r'Demo pair (\d) (input|output) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):', log)]
# only first occurrences (offsets < 300000)
lab = [l for l in labels if l[0] < 300000]
print(lab)

def get_grid(start, h, w):
    # text right after the header line
    body = log[start:start+6000]
    lines = body.split('\\n')[1:]
    rows = []
    for ln in lines:
        toks = ln.split()
        if len(toks) == w and all(t.isdigit() for t in toks):
            rows.append([int(t) for t in toks])
        if len(rows) == h: break
    return rows

grids = {}
for (off,k,kind) in [(l[0],l[1],l[2]) for l in lab]:
    m = re.match(r'.*\((\d+)x(\d+)\)', log[off:off+60])
    pass
import re as _re
for m2 in _re.finditer(r'Demo pair (\d) (input|output) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):', log[:300000]):
    k, kind, h, w = m2.group(1), m2.group(2), int(m2.group(3)), int(m2.group(4))
    grids[(k,kind)] = get_grid(m2.end(), h, w)
    print(k, kind, h, w, 'rows got:', len(grids[(k,kind)]))
# test input
m2 = _re.search(r'Test input \(24x28\):', log[:300000])
T = get_grid(m2.end(), 24, 28)
print('test rows', len(T))
import pickle
pickle.dump({'grids':grids,'test':T}, open('/tmp/all.pkl','wb'))

for m2 in re.finditer(r'Demo pair (\d) (input|output) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):', log):
    k, kind, hh, ww = m2.group(1), m2.group(2), int(m2.group(3)), int(m2.group(4))
    if (k,kind) not in grids:
        grids[(k,kind)] = get_grid(m2.end(), hh, ww)
        print(k, kind, hh, ww, len(grids[(k,kind)]))

def analyze2(k):
    gi = grids[(k,'input')]; go = grids[(k,'output')]
    H, W = len(gi), len(gi[0])
    cnt = Counter(v for row in gi for v in row)
    # line rows: rows where the most common value is rare overall
    # line color = value whose rows are full
    linecands = [c for c in cnt if sum(gi[r][cc]==c for r in range(H) for cc in range(W) if r%1==0)]
    # find rows fully covered by top-2 colors? Use: a line row has <=2 distinct values and repeats
    lr = [r for r in range(H) if len(set(gi[r]))<=2 and len(set(gi[r]))<=2]
    print(f'--- demo {k}: {H}x{W}, counts {dict(cnt)}')
    for r,row in enumerate(gi): print(r, row)
    print('output:', go)
analyze2('1'); analyze2('2'); analyze2('3')

def detect_lines(gi, thr=0.5):
    H,W = gi.shape
    cnt = Counter(int(x) for x in gi.flat)
    def ap_ok(vals):
        if len(vals) < 2: return False
        d = vals[1]-vals[0]
        return d >= 2 and all(vals[i+1]-vals[i]==d for i in range(len(vals)-1))
    for c in cnt:
        rows_c = [r for r in range(H) if sum(1 for cc in range(W) if gi[r,cc]==c)/W >= thr]
        cols_c = [cc for cc in range(W) if sum(1 for r in range(H) if gi[r,cc]==c)/H >= thr]
        if ap_ok(rows_c) and ap_ok(cols_c):
            return c, rows_c, cols_c
    return None, None, None

def solve(k, verbose=True):
    gi = np.array(grids[(k,'input')]); go = np.array(grids[(k,'output')])
    lc, R, C = detect_lines(gi)
    cnt = Counter(int(x) for x in gi.flat)
    interior = cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    m = np.array([[int(gi[r][c]) for c in C] for r in R])
    nR, nC = len(R)-1, len(C)-1
    out = np.full((nR,nC), interior, dtype=int)
    for i in range(nR):
        for j in range(nC):
            cs = [m[i][j], m[i][j+1], m[i+1][j], m[i+1][j+1]]
            if len(set(cs))==1 and cs[0] != lc:
                out[i][j] = cs[0]
    ok = (out==go).all()
    print(f'demo {k}: line={lc} R={R} C={C} interior={interior} {"MATCH" if ok else "MISMATCH"}')
    if verbose and not ok: print('pred:', out.tolist()); print('actual:', go.tolist())
    return ok, lc, interior

for k in ['1','2','3']: solve(k)
